summary: Preinstall fetches Bun runtime to execute obfuscated sibling payload
details: @servicetitan/marketing-ui@9.3.6 declares preinstall=`node setup.mjs`. setup.mjs is obfuscator.io-style (`_0x…` identifiers) and, at install time, downloads a platform-specific Bun runtime ZIP from https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v<version>/<archive>.zip, extracts it to a temporary directory, chmods it executable, and invokes it (execFileSync) against sibling file math_init.js. math_init.js is a ~727 KB `@bun @bun-cjs` bundle with a rotated string-array decoder (`WV8StW`), a large charcode lookup table (`n7gIxM`), a custom decode routine (`hc1jfK9`), and hex-named identifiers; it is unreachable under plain Node and is not part of the shipped React component API (main is dist/index.js). A React marketing-UI library has no legitimate reason to fetch a second language runtime at install to execute an opaque bundled payload — this is the alternate-runtime dropper pattern, giving the publisher arbitrary code execution on every installer's machine at `npm install` time and bypassing normal Node lifecycle inspection.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
